observed.input_line: I still stumble over calling myself a manager. At today's team introduction I nearly said designer again, even though I like the new work. Could we think about why naming a new role feels so awkward, and find an introduction that feels honest to me?

context_resolution.explanation: No confirmed book or reading boundary yet; Muse will call librarian_route during its own turn if the request appears to depend on a specific book.

observed.reply:
The awkwardness doesn’t mean you’re being dishonest—you already know that you like the new work. One possibility is that the old title still comes more automatically, while the new one hasn’t become easy to say yet. Another is that “manager” carries expectations you’re still deciding how to make your own. You don’t have to settle that whole question before introducing yourself.

Here are a few honest options:

- “Hi, I’m [name]. I’m a manager, and I’m enjoying the new work.”
- “Hi, I’m [name]. I recently moved into management, and I’m glad to be here.”
- “Hi, I’m [name]. I’m in a management role now—I’m still getting used to saying that.”
- “Hi, I’m [name]. I’m a manager, and I also come from a design background.”

The last one lets “manager” be true without pretending “designer” has disappeared. When you imagine saying the title, what feels most awkward: claiming it, being seen differently because of it, or leaving the old label out?

output.reply:
That awkwardness makes sense: “designer” is a role you’ve practiced naming, while “manager” may still feel new enough that saying it out loud makes the transition feel more real. You don’t have to reject the old identity to make room for the new one—and liking the new work doesn’t require feeling completely fluent in the title yet.

You could try an introduction that is accurate but not overdramatic:

- “Hi, I’m [name]. I’m a manager, and I’m enjoying the new work.”
- “Hi, I’m [name]. I recently moved into management, and I’m glad to be here.”
- “Hi, I’m [name]. I’m working in a management role now; I’m still getting used to saying that.”

The third is especially honest if you want to acknowledge the awkwardness rather than hide it. Which part feels most uncomfortable: claiming the title itself, leaving “designer” behind, or saying it in front of other people?
